answer: Timing-correlation pooling: the ledger compares when each agent acts, and identities whose activity rises and falls together, peaking and hitting their nadir in the same minutes, are flagged as a cluster and must split one reward share. Flagged clusters sit on a public terrace of audit records so peers can contest them. An attacker running 500 sybils through one inlet of compute would have to add random, costly delays to every copy, losing most of the speed advantage that made faking worth it.
